evidence.quote: I agree that the balance sheet needs to shrink but, as I will show, not by as much as some believe it should.
I believe we can likely continue to let a share of maturing and prepaying securities roll off our balance sheet for some time, reducing reserve balances.
We have far too many long-term assets on our balance sheet relative to my arguments for how to structure the balance sheet.
We are reducing the size of the balance sheet slowly and need to consider shifting it toward more bills.
So, the Fed can provide all the liquidity that banks need at zero marginal cost, which makes me wonder why some want to make reserves scarce.

parsed.rationale: The speech is purely about balance sheet structure, supporting continued runoff and a shift toward shorter-duration assets, a mild hawkish lean on the balance sheet, though it argues against shrinking as far as critics want. It offers no views on rates, inflation, or activity, so the overall stance is near neutral.
